title: India and Japan hold fourth 2+2 ministerial dialogue in Tokyo
summary: The defence and foreign ministers of India and Japan met in Tokyo for the fourth 2+2 dialogue.
body: India and Japan held their fourth 2+2 ministerial meeting in Tokyo on 19 November 2026. The format brings together both countries' defence and foreign ministers.
India holds 2+2 dialogues with a small group of close partners, including the USA, Japan and Australia. The format is used to align defence and foreign policy, especially on the Indo-Pacific.

- Both are members of the Quad, with the USA and Australia.
- JIMEX is the India–Japan naval exercise; Dharma Guardian is the Army exercise.
- Japan is a major partner in Indian infrastructure, including the Mumbai–Ahmedabad high-speed rail project.
interview: Why is Japan important to India's Indo-Pacific strategy?
